summary: Math.abs returns a number’s absolute value, removing its sign.
documentation: Math.abs returns a number’s absolute value, removing its sign. Subtracting two measurements and taking the absolute value gives their nonnegative distance on a number line without requiring a particular input order.
inputs: An array of pairs of small finite numbers.
returns: The absolute difference for each pair.
caution: Math.abs can coerce nonnumeric inputs. This task supplies numbers only; real form input needs deliberate parsing and finite-value validation.
scenarios: Compare a measured dimension with its target tolerance.
Report the magnitude of a signed stock-count discrepancy.
Show a coordinate distance along one axis in a layout tool.
title: Measure absolute differences
problem: For each pair [actual, target], return the nonnegative difference magnitude. Values and differences are finite, with magnitude below one million. Preserve pair order.
hint: Subtract the pair’s values before applying Math.abs.
goal: Use Math.abs() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
